registry_info.name: noise_quarry
registry_info.description: A synthesis artifact for the `readout` family's B dialect (relief · plate · column). One scalar field, evaluated once at build time and cut three ways, so the three conventions can be measured against each other instead of met one at a time in six rooms.
registry_info.note: Per-token registry file so parallel builders never share one JSON. The three lane names are PRELOADED from ProfileRandom.gd at runtime and validated at _ready in both directions; do not retype them here or in the script.

noise_quarry.name: Noise Quarry
noise_quarry.description: One field, quarried. A single 24 x 24 gradient-noise field is evaluated ONCE at build time and cut into three benches standing side by side on one apron: relief reads each sample as elevation and stands as a crust; plate reads it as an image and lies flat at the datum, the value surviving only as colour; column reads it as a measured quantity and stands a bar from the floor. The same 576 numbers, three bodies. `octaves` changes how many scales are summed into the one field; `evidence` changes how much proof is standing that the three bodies are the same numbers — nothing, a datum rule across all three, or the back wall ruled in three sections, each in its own convention. The three rulings do not agree about where zero is, and that disagreement is the artifact. Nothing animates, nothing is grabbable, nothing is random.
interactions: stand square to the wall and read the three zeros: the relief's is the middle tick, the column's is the bottom one, and the plate has none
put the relief's silhouette against the column's skyline — they are the same line, because a bar's top IS the crust's height
find the sample the plate cannot tell you: every tile on the middle bench is at the same height
switch octaves from 4 to 1 and watch which bench loses the most
noise_quarry.qfep_connection: Three conventions for one field, and no neutral one among them. Each spends the sample on a different property — position, colour, extent — and each pays somewhere else: the relief hides its own low ground, the column rectifies every negative into a positive length, and the plate hides nothing and can measure nothing. The `plate` section of the ruled wall is the artifact's own dark spot: a scale with no levels on it, standing between two scales that have them, so the absence is a mark rather than an omission.
noise_quarry.relationships: Synthesised from the eight registry names that declare the B dialect of `readout` (mandelbrot_set, complexity_pattern, perlin_noise, perlin_noise_terrain, random_edge_profile, simplex_noise, and noisesphere/noisetorus which drop `column`). Replaces none of them and re-runs none of their axes from the outside. Sibling in argument to slack_yard, which makes the same move for the `slack` family.

spatial_needs.footprint_note: The apron is 4.20 m across the three benches by 2.17 m from the ruled wall to the front edge, so a 5 x 3 clear patch. The lane names are lettered on the apron's +Z edge, the datum rule stands at +Z and the ruled wall closes the -Z side, so the artifact reads correctly approached from +Z; `orientation: face_approach` plus a rotation in the map token is how you get that. `wall_backing` is true because the artifact BRINGS its own back wall and should not be given a second one 0.4 m behind it. There is no collider anywhere in the file, so the pathfinder will route straight through the benches — correct, because there are no benches, there is a picture of three.

measurements.measured_by: computed from the script's own layout constants and re-derived in a Python replica of the same geometry; no Godot was run, per the brief. MeshInstance3D only, which is what the capture AABB counts: two BoxMesh slabs (apron, wall), the datum rule, up to 22 rule marks and three SurfaceTool benches, all MeshInstance3D. There is no MultiMeshInstance3D and no CSG, so no `layers = 0` anchor is needed and none is present; the three Label3D lane tabs are not MeshInstance3D and do not enter the box. X = 3 x 1.20 benches + 2 x 0.18 gaps + 2 x 0.12 apron margin = 4.20. Z = -1.27 (apron behind the wall) to +0.90 (apron front edge) = 2.17. Y = 0 (apron underside, so the grid's base-to-floor grounding is a no-op and no auto_ground opt-out is needed) to 0.60 = the topmost wall tick, whose centre sits at DATUM + AMP = 0.58 and whose half-height is 0.020.

dna.axis_shape:
BOTH AXES NEST, and both nestings are provable from the code rather than asserted.

`evidence` nests in the ordinary way: result is contained in trace is contained in longhand. _build() adds the datum rule under `if evidence == "trace" or evidence == "longhand"` and the wall rulings under `if evidence == "longhand"`; no rung removes a mark an earlier rung drew, and the three bodies are identical at all three. It must be swept in order and its tail is a ceiling, not a case.

`octaves` nests too, and more literally than a ladder usually does: the K-octave field is the K-1-octave field plus one more term of the same sum. _compute_field() accumulates s += amp * _perlin(...) with amp halving each pass, so octave 4 is octave 3 with 0.125 of amplitude added on top. The ONE thing that is not nested is the normaliser — the sum is divided by the sum of the amplitudes it actually used, which differs per rung — and that is deliberate: it keeps every rung at full range so the fixed colour ceiling and the fixed 2 x AMP gauge mean the same thing in all four frames. Without it the K=1 field would occupy 53% of the gauge and the K=4 field 100%, and the axis would be measuring loudness rather than detail.

THE FAMILY WORD IS NEITHER, WHICH IS WHY IT IS NOT AN AXIS. `relief`, `plate` and `column` sit SIDE BY SIDE: NoiseVisualizer._shape_cube writes three mutually exclusive assignments of one sample (size + position.y = value; size + position.y = 0; size.y = value + amplitude + position.y = height/2) and no branch contains another. complexity_pattern is the same shape in different numbers, MandelbrotSet._apply_readout the same in a MultiMesh. Parallel values are exactly the case where showing them all at once is NOT merely the top value, so the word is exhibited and the axes vary the field instead.
dna.default:
evidence=longhand, octaves=4.

A SYNTHESIS HAS NO SHIPPED PLACEMENTS, so there is nothing to preserve and the default is a free design choice; the rule that outranks everything in doc/DNA_PROMOTION_BRIEF.md governs promotions of placed artifacts and has no work to do here. That freedom is spent on the strongest single reading rather than the emptiest.

WHY `longhand` AND NOT `result`. `result` is the emptiest rung by definition — three bodies and no way to say they are the same numbers, which is a picture of three sculptures rather than of an argument. `longhand` is the only rung where the artifact's actual claim is legible without a caption: three rulings of one field, side by side on one wall, disagreeing about where zero is. A visitor who meets only the default meets the finding. `trace` is one token away and is the right value for a room that wants the bodies to dominate.

WHY `4` AND NOT `1`. 4 is what every member of this family actually ships — NoiseVisualizer sets fractal_octaves from a slider whose default is 4, simplex_noise declares `@export_range(1, 8, 1) var octaves: int = 4` because 4 was its hard-coded value, and noise_space defaults to 4 as well. It is also the rung where the three conventions are furthest apart in what they cost: at one octave the field is a single smooth swell and all three bodies read it about equally well, which makes for a handsome frame and a weak argument.

DECLARATION ORDER IS LOAD-BEARING, and it is why `evidence` is listed first. build_dna_gallery.sweep walks the axes in declaration order and trims the LATER one from the tail of its value list until the cross product fits the cap. At the gallery's default --max=9 a 3 x 4 declaration renders as evidence(3) x octaves(3): all three evidence rungs survive and octaves is trimmed to [1, 2, 3], which is still a real ladder. Declared the other way round it would have rendered octaves(4) x evidence(2) and dropped `longhand` — the default, and the only rung that carries the finding. THE FULL SHEET NEEDS --max=12.
dna.was: did not exist. Nothing was promoted here and no shipped behaviour was touched. This is the cross-member argument the eighteen `readout` declarations leave unbuilt: six of them describe relief, plate and column as three claims about one field, and not one of them can stand two of the three at once, because a body can only be shaped one way at a time.
dna.kin:
THE WORD IS TWO QUESTIONS, AND THE REGISTRY HAS TO SAY SO. `readout` is declared by eighteen artifacts in what is really five vocabularies over two questions:

  A. none | numeral | gradation | lattice — 9 members: health_display, hits_reset_display, line_interface, xyz_coordinates, qfep_calibrator, qfep_reactor, lambda_promenade, and xyz_slider_plate + line, which declare it numeral-first because that is their own default hoisted to the head of the list. HOW IS A VALUE DISPLAYED — not at all, as a number, as a continuous ramp, as a discrete grid. The subject is ONE SCALAR and the values are apparatus hung beside it. This dialect has an owner: commons/primitives/point/xyz_slider_plate.gd holds the canon, a READOUT_ALIASES table and a static readout_name(), and line.gd parses through it, so those two cannot drift.

  B. relief | plate | column — 6 members: mandelbrot_set, complexity_pattern, perlin_noise, perlin_noise_terrain, random_edge_profile, simplex_noise. Plus noisesphere and noisetorus, which declare relief | plate | none and say why in their own comments: 'column is the family value a closed surface cannot build (nowhere to stand a bar)'. HOW IS A SCALAR FIELD EMBODIED — as a displaced surface, as a flat image, as extruded bars. The subject is A WHOLE FIELD and the values are three bodies.

  C. entropy_jar alone: figures | number | verdict | none.

Reading out a VALUE and embodying a FIELD are not the same question, and one word over both is the messiest thing in this corpus's vocabulary. This quarry takes dialect B, because it holds a field. It does not touch dialect A and does not propose renaming anything: the two dialects are recorded here so the next agent meets the split instead of discovering it.

DIALECT B HAS NO OWNER, WHICH IS THE DRIFT RISK. Where dialect A forwards through one static function, dialect B carries FIVE byte-identical copies of the same array — MandelbrotSet.gd:62, terrain_generator.gd:63, ProfileRandom.gd:76, complexity_pattern.gd:108 (untyped) and the two sphere/torus variants — and no alias table anywhere. Checked character for character: the four full-dialect consts are identical, and the two closed-surface ones differ only in their third value. So the vocabulary has NOT drifted yet; it simply has nothing stopping it.

WHAT THIS QUARRY DOES ABOUT IT. noise_quarry.gd opens with
  const READOUT_SRC := preload("res://algorithms/randomness/ProfileRandom.gd")
and every lane comes out of READOUT_SRC.READOUTS at build time — the benches, their order, their count and their lettering are the family's array, not a copy of it. ProfileRandom.gd is the one read because it is the only member of the five whose script parses with NO external dependency at all: no class_name, no preload, no reference to a global class. terrain_generator.gd was the other candidate and was passed over for a mechanical reason — it is `class_name PerlinTerrainGenerator` and calls MeshHelper and NoiseHelper, so preloading it would put two more scripts between this artifact and its own vocabulary. _check_family_list() runs at _ready and push_errors in both directions: a value the family declares that this quarry has no builder for, and a builder this quarry has that the family has dropped.

`evidence` IS THE FAMILY WORD, TAKEN WITH A SUB-LIST THAT ALREADY EXISTS. 45 artifacts declare `evidence`; 28 carry result | trace | longhand | axiom and SIX carry exactly result | trace | longhand, in that order. This takes the three-rung list, character for character and in the siblings' order, and refuses `axiom` on the record (see dna.declines).

`octaves` IS THE FAMILY WORD AND ITS LIST HAS ALREADY DRIFTED. Two members declare it and they disagree: noise_space says [1, 2, 3, 4] and simplex_noise says [1, 2, 4, 6]. noise_space's own comment gives its reason — its base wavelength is about 2 m against a mesh sampled every 0.1 m, so octave 5 lands below the mesh's Nyquist wavelength and rungs 5 and 6 'add aliasing at a sixteenth of the amplitude and nothing a still frame can distinguish from 4'. That reason is a property of the GRID, not of the word, so it was re-derived here rather than inherited:

  This quarry's bench is 1.20 m across sampled at GRID = 24, i.e. every 0.050 m.
  SPAN = 1.0, so octave k has a lattice cell of 1.20 / 2^(k-1) metres:
    k=1  1.200 m = 24.0 sample cells
    k=2  0.600 m = 12.0
    k=3  0.300 m =  6.0
    k=4  0.150 m =  3.0
    k=5  0.075 m =  1.5   <- below the 2-cell Nyquist wavelength
    k=6  0.0375 m = 0.75
  So the ladder stops at 4 on this grid, independently, and takes noise_space's list.

WHAT SIMPLEX_NOISE'S LIST WOULD HAVE COST. To make a rung named 6 resolve at three sample cells the grid would have to be GRID >= 3 * 2^5 = 96, i.e. a cell of 0.0125 m, which at this sweep's 139.90 px/m projects to 1.42 screen pixels along the frame's long axis. The finer ladder is only available on a grid whose cells are invisible, which is the same trade noise_space made and the reason its list is the honest one for a still.
declines: `readout` AS THIS ARTIFACT'S AXIS. Refused for the reason slack_yard refused `slack`, and stated here so nobody reopens it: every one of the eight B-dialect members uses the word to stand in ONE convention and forgo the other two, so an axis over it would have three values each of which demolishes two thirds of this exhibit, and the big number it produced would measure the exhibit being dismantled. The three values sit SIDE BY SIDE — a lifted cube is not a flat cube with something added, and a bar is not a deeper lift — which is precisely the condition under which showing them all at once is not merely the top value. The quarry takes that: it stands all three and varies the FIELD. The word is exhibited, lettered on the apron at the head of each bench, and read out of the family's own const rather than retyped.

`axiom`, THE FOURTH RUNG OF `evidence`. In the 28 artifacts that carry the full list, axiom is the textbook line INSTEAD OF the demonstration — slope_tangent_demo's axiom plate draws no tangent at all, velocity_arrow's states v = dP/dt and draws no arrow. The equivalent here would be a plate reading 'one field, three bodies' with the three bodies gone, and there is nothing left to photograph: the quarry's claim is not a statable identity, it is that three embodiments of one field differ, which cannot be asserted in a line without becoming the thing it denies. Taking a word without its answers is the folding_past fault, so the three-rung sub-list six siblings already carry is taken instead, and the refusal is recorded rather than papered over.

`generator` (simplex | perlin | value | cellular, 4 members). It was the obvious first axis and it is refused on both grounds. First, the brief's own design line is ONE field evaluated once and cut N ways; four bases would be four fields and four quarries. Second, and decisive: in all four members that declare it the word names a FastNoiseLite noise type, and this artifact's basis is a hand-written integer-hash gradient noise. Calling that `perlin` would be taking a word and giving it a different answer. The basis here is fixed and unswept and no basis vocabulary is claimed. The hand-written basis is not a preference — it is what makes dna.predicted_degeneracy below arithmetic instead of an estimate, because FastNoiseLite's fractal normalisation cannot be reproduced offline.

`assay` (none | gauge | control | chart | vitrine, 19 artifacts), the near miss for `evidence`. It is the softbody bench family's word for apparatus placed AROUND A SPECIMEN, and petri_dish_worms defines `control` as 'a second, identical, EMPTY dish'. This quarry has no case to be a vitrine and no empty duplicate to be a control; taking the word would force two of its five rungs to mean something here or force them to be dropped, and dropping rungs from a nineteen-artifact word is exactly the drift the corpus keeps catching.

AN OCCLUSION LEDGER, designed, computed and cut. The plan was a bar per bench counting how many of the 576 samples that body hides from the standpoint — a real count, exactly the kind law 6 asks for, and the honest way to say what each convention costs. It was dropped when the arithmetic came back: the relief's crust and the column's bar tops are THE SAME LOCUS by construction (a bar's top is at DATUM + AMP * h, which is where the crust's tile is), so a horizon walk over the two returns nearly the same count, differing only by whatever squeezes through the 0.010 m gaps between bars. Two of the three bars would have been the same length and the third zero, and a viewer would have read 'relief and column are the same convention', which is false. The finding survives in prose: the two bodies hide the same samples and differ in what they are solid to.

A FRAME-RELATIVE CEILING ANYWHERE. The colour ramp runs h = -1 .. +1 on all three bodies at every rung of `octaves`; the wall's ruled span is 2 x AMP metres at every rung; the five levels are at h = -1, -0.5, 0, +0.5, +1 in both ruled sections. A blue tile means the same number on the plate at one octave as on the relief at four. The consequence is visible and is left alone: the realised field spans 1.796 of the available 2.0 at K=1 and 1.425 at K=4, so the high rungs genuinely use less of the gauge. sorting_hall normalised each frame to its own busiest row and its gauge then said nothing about the quantity it existed to show.

ANY ANIMATION, RATE, DURATION OR DECAY. A noise field has obvious time-domain axes — the third coordinate as a clock, a scroll, an octave fading in — and every one of them is invisible to a still PNG. Two of this family's members had to export a freeze for exactly this reason (terrain_generator's `animate`, MandelbrotSet's `freeze_pulse`). There is no _process, no _physics_process, no Timer, no Tween and no physics body anywhere in this file, so there is nothing to freeze.
dna.predicted_degeneracy:
PREDICTED BEFORE ANY CAPTURE, in the critic's own currency rather than in changed pixels, because a prediction in the wrong units is a prediction about a different instrument. The critic crops to the union of the two frames' subject boxes, neutralises each frame's own background, converts to greyscale, RESIZES TO 160 x 160 and takes the mean of the hottest 5%. The numbers below come from building this exact geometry in Python — the same hash, the same fBm, the same layout constants — rasterising it with a z-buffer at this exact camera (FOV 34, PAD 1.9, yaw 0.62, pitch -0.26, 760 x 760, dna.framing 0.60) and pushing the result through that same pipeline.

THE CLOSEST PAIR IS `octaves` 3 <-> 4, AT evidence=longhand: 8.12% focus, 0.62% frame, on a crop of 652 x 240 px. Per channel the same pair reads 10.29%, so it should clear the critic's TWIN_FOCUS bar of 6% in both currencies and should NOT appear in the twins list.

WHY THAT PAIR, arithmetically. The field is fBm at persistence 0.5, so octave k carries amplitude 0.5^(k-1) against a normaliser of the sum:
    K=2  last octave = 0.500 / 1.500 = 33.33% of the sum
    K=3  last octave = 0.250 / 1.750 = 14.29%
    K=4  last octave = 0.125 / 1.875 =  6.67%
Measured over the 576 samples, the mean absolute change in h and the mean vertical move it produces at AMP = 0.24:
    1 -> 2   mean |dh| 0.2708   max 0.6498   65.0 mm
    2 -> 3   mean |dh| 0.0818   max 0.2325   19.6 mm
    3 -> 4   mean |dh| 0.0335   max 0.1100    8.0 mm
    1 -> 4   mean |dh| 0.3191   max 0.9266   76.6 mm
Adjacent rungs converge geometrically, so the top of the ladder is where the axis is thinnest. This is the field_room ruling and not a fault to fix: the rung is thin because the thing it describes is thin, and padding it would mean raising persistence away from the family's 0.5 to make a louder picture of a different function.

THE WHOLE PREDICTED SHEET, focus %, at each of the three evidence rungs (longhand / trace / result):
    octaves 3<->4    8.12  8.21  8.30
    octaves 2<->3   10.04 10.16 10.43
    octaves 2<->4   10.59 10.79 11.06
    octaves 1<->2   12.07 12.60 12.99
    octaves 1<->3   13.08 13.67 14.01
    octaves 1<->4   13.21 13.90 14.24
and, at each of the four octave rungs (1 / 2 / 3 / 4):
    evidence result<->trace       8.25  8.61  8.77  8.73
    evidence trace<->longhand    17.34 17.51 17.50 17.50
    evidence result<->longhand   18.41 18.76 18.75 18.74
AXIS MEANS: `evidence` 1.15% frame / 14.90% focus -> BITES. `octaves` 1.05% frame / 11.53% focus -> WEAK, one third of a point under the critic's 12% bar, and stated as WEAK in advance rather than discovered afterwards.

THE PREDICTION IS A NEAR DEAD HEAT AND IS OFFERED AS ONE. The three thinnest pairs in the sheet are 8.12, 8.21 and 8.25 — the first two are `octaves` 3<->4 and the third is `evidence` result<->trace at octaves=1. Thirteen hundredths of a point separates the predicted winner from a pair on the OTHER AXIS. Godot's showcase key light and its specular fringe are not in the replica, and either could move a pair by more than that. So: the closest pair is predicted to be `octaves` 3<->4, and if it comes back as `evidence` result<->trace instead, the prediction is not wrong, it is resolved — and what it resolves is whether a 3.96 m x 0.09 m blade appearing counts for more or less than every sample in three benches moving 8 mm.

SOMETHING THIS PREDICTION ALREADY CAUGHT, which is the reason for making it. The first build marked five sample stations with 0.040 m probes rising through each body to a head above it, and a hand estimate put result<->trace near 7% focus. Rasterised, it measured 1.15-1.57% — INERT territory, five times below the estimate — and looking at the PNG showed why: the probe rods run from the apron up THROUGH the crust and the bar field, so everything except the head is inside the body it is marking. Marks behind the furniture, which is operations_gallery's fault in a different costume. The stations were replaced by the datum rule and the ruled wall, and the same pair now measures 8.25-8.77%. Nothing else in the chain would have objected: fifteen orange dabs on a 4.68 m subject compile, gate, sweep and photograph exactly like an honest axis.

AND ONE PAIR PREDICTED **NOT** TO BE DEGENERATE, because it looks like it should be. The relief bench and the column bench have IDENTICAL top surfaces by construction — a bar's top sits at DATUM + AMP * h, which is exactly where the crust's tile stands — so from directly above they are the same picture. They are not a degenerate pair here and never appear as one, because `readout` is not swept: both stand in every frame, and what separates them is what they are solid to, which is only legible from an oblique standpoint. If a future probe from overhead reports the two benches as identical, that is the correct reading of an overhead view and not a fault.

WHAT WOULD FALSIFY THIS.
(a) If any `evidence` pair reads 0.00%, run tools/check_dna_declarations.py --token=noise_quarry first — a value the code cannot reach falls back to the default and prints identical tiles.
(b) If `octaves` comes back near 0% while `evidence` bites, the field is not being rebuilt: apply_grid_config only calls _build() when a value actually changed AND _built is true, so a sweep that sets octaves before _ready and again after would be a no-op the second time and correct the first.
(c) If BOTH axes come back roughly 1.5x these numbers, the cause is SHADING, and the difference is known rather than suspected. The replica renders hard-edged untextured colour with a single Lambert term, no shadows, and — this is the part that matters — the ABSOLUTE value of n.L, so a face pointing away from the key is lit as brightly as one facing it. The shipped artifact passes explicit outward normals into every quad and disables culling, so in Godot the faces pointing away from the key (0.47 of the light is along -x, and the frame's long axis is +x) go dark instead. The bars' +x sides and the crust's east-facing skirts are where the two will disagree most, and both are exactly where `octaves` does its work, so the replica's `octaves` figure is the more likely of the two to be low.
(d) The replica does not model the three Label3D lane tabs. They are constant across all twelve tiles and add roughly 0.5% more constant subject area to every crop, which dilutes both axis means slightly — in the direction of the numbers above being a little high, not a little low.
dna.framing_why:
DERIVED FROM THE UNION AABB ACROSS ALL TWELVE FRAMES, not from the default. Union 4.20 x 0.60 x 2.17 (x across the three benches, z from the ruled wall to the apron's front edge); diagonal sqrt(17.64 + 0.36 + 4.7089) = 4.7654, radius 2.3827. The rig is dist = radius / tan(FOV/2) x PAD x framing with FOV 34 and PAD 1.9, so framing 1.0 would put the camera at 2.3827 / 0.305731 x 1.9 = 14.8075 m and show a 9.0543 m frame around a 4.20 m object — PAD 1.9 already shows 1.9x the bounding radius, which is why a bench object wants framing well below 1.0.

AT 0.60 the camera comes to 8.8845 m and the frame to 5.4325 m, which is 139.90 px per metre. The subject's projected width is 4.20 x |right.x| + 2.17 x |right.z| = 4.20 x 0.81388 + 2.17 x 0.58104 = 3.4183 + 1.2609 = 4.6791 m, i.e. 86.1% of frame width, with 38 px of clear margin each side. Rasterised at that setting the subject covers 16.20% of the frame — far above the ~6% dilution floor and above the blank-render check. Cropping is arithmetically impossible above framing = 1 / PAD = 0.5263 because the rig fits by bounding SPHERE, so 0.60 keeps 14% of sphere margin in hand; 0.55 was measured too (93.9% of frame width, 19 px of margin) and rejected as too little slack for the showcase key light's specular fringe, which the replica does not model.

WHY THE UNION AND NOT THE DEFAULT: the ruled wall exists at every value of `evidence`, but at `longhand` its topmost tick raises the box from 0.58 to 0.60, and the datum rule adds nothing to the extent at all. The apron is the full 4.20 x 2.17 at every value of both axes, so the box does not move between tiles for any other reason and all twelve are framed identically.

GAUGE CHECK AT 139.90 px/m, because foresight_range shipped 0.028 m arrows onto an 18 m lane and sorting_hall drew a whole axis three pixels wide. Screen sizes use |right.x| = 0.81388 and |right.z| = 0.58104 along the frame's long axis and cos(pitch) = 0.96639 for verticals:
  datum rule    3.96 m long -> 450.9 px;  0.090 m tall -> 12.2 px
  wall tick     1.20 m long -> 136.7 px;  0.040 m tall ->  5.4 px
  zero tick     1.20 m long -> 136.7 px;  0.072 m tall ->  9.7 px
  ramp band     1.20 m long -> 136.7 px;  0.040 m tall ->  5.4 px
  ruled span    0.48 m tall ->  64.9 px
  crust lip     0.035 m     ->   4.7 px
  sample cell   0.050 m     ->   5.7 px along x, 4.1 px along z
  bar gap       0.010 m     ->   1.1 px along x, 0.8 px along z
THE TICKS WERE RESIZED FOR THE BENCH, NOT FOR THE EYE. The critic crops to about 652 x 240 and resizes to 160 x 160, so verticals are downsampled 1.5x and a mark must clear about 4.5 screen pixels to survive as three samples. The first build's ticks were 0.022 m = 3.0 px = 2 samples, which is sorting_hall's three-pixel gauge exactly; 0.040 m gives 5.4 px = 3.6 samples, and the zero tick 9.7 px = 6.5.

THE BAR GAP IS BELOW A PIXEL AND IS LEFT THERE. At 0.010 m the gaps between the column's bars are 1.1 px wide, so at this framing the column bench reads as stepped mass rather than as countable bars, and the two conventions it is being compared against are legible at the same distance. Widening it would mean either a coarser grid — which caps the octave ladder at 3, see dna.kin — or narrower bars, which is the same dilution in the other direction. The bar field is legible AS A FIELD, which is what the axis needs; the countability of individual bars is a nicety of the convention and is genuinely lost at this range, which is stated rather than pretended away.

THE WALL'S STANDOFF WAS PART OF THE FRAMING DECISION. At the sweep's standpoint a sight line descends 0.3268 m per metre of ground travel, so a wall behind the benches is grazed by their own back rows. At 0.55 m of standoff the clearance is 0.1797 m: the plate bench, whose back row sits at DATUM = 0.34 exactly, hides the wall below y = 0.1603, which is the bottom 12.6% of the 0.48 m ruled span — about one and a half of the plate's twelve colour bands. Less standoff was measured and costs more of the ramp; more standoff costs frame width, because it lengthens the only dimension that was already the second largest. The first build put a separate ruled board behind each bench at 0.06 m of standoff and lost 55% of every one of them, which is why there is now one wall and it stands well back.
dna.fixture_note:
NO FIXTURE AND NO SEED KEY IS NEEDED, and it is checkable rather than claimed. The file contains no randf, no randi, no randomize, no RandomNumberGenerator, no _process, no _physics_process, no Timer, no Tween, no physics body and no reference to the scene tree outside its own children. The field comes from a 32-bit integer hash of the lattice coordinates with a compile-time seed, masked to 0xFFFFFFFF at every step, so it has no state at all and two captures of one value are two photographs of one object. _ready is ungated: it reads config metadata, validates the family list and builds the whole quarry standalone, so the sweep's rescue path (call apply_grid_config when the AABB measures zero) will never fire.

THREE WAYS IN, ONE DOOR EACH. The sweep sets the @export directly before add_child; the grid stamps config_evidence / config_octaves metadata, which _read_grid_config_meta walks the ancestor chain for before _ready builds; and apply_grid_config takes a dictionary. All three are validated against _is_evidence / _valid_octaves, and apply_grid_config rebuilds ONLY when a value actually changed AND _ready has already built once — the force_pad fault. An unrecognised word or an out-of-range integer keeps the standing value.

NEITHER AXIS IS A BOOL, so the fixture-string trap (a typed bool rejecting the string "true" before _ready) cannot occur here. `octaves` is an int and is read through int(), which accepts the string "3" a sweep would set.
dna.still_note:
WHAT SHOULD BITE AND WHAT SHOULD NOT, said in advance so a thin number is read correctly.

CONSTANT AT EVERY VALUE OF `evidence`, by construction: the apron, the ruled wall's blank stone, the three lane tabs and all three bodies. Everything that changes between the three tiles is proof apparatus, which is the axis's whole subject.

CONSTANT AT EVERY VALUE OF `octaves`: the apron, the wall, the tabs, the datum rule and the wall's rulings — the ruled span is 2 x AMP metres and the five levels are at fixed h, so the gauge does not move when the field does. Everything inside the three benches changes. `octaves` should be the larger frame number and the smaller focus number, and it is: 1.05% frame against `evidence`'s 1.15%, but 11.53% focus against 14.90%. That inversion is the honest shape of the two axes — one repaints a wide thin subject everywhere, the other adds bright localised apparatus — and if it comes back the other way round, the field is not being rebuilt.

TWO BENCHES THAT SHARE A SURFACE, AND IT IS NOT A FAULT: the relief's crust and the column's bar tops are the same locus, because a bar's height is (h + 1) x AMP measured up from Y_FLOOR and the crust's tile is at DATUM + AMP x h, and DATUM = Y_FLOOR + AMP. They still LOOK different (one is a skin with a 0.035 m lip, the other is solid to the floor) and they are ruled differently on the wall. Do not 'fix' it. It is the exhibit's best single sentence: two conventions that agree exactly about where every sample is and disagree completely about what is underneath it.

NO TEXT NAMES AN AXIS VALUE. There are three Label3D in the artifact and they letter the three conventions — relief, plate, column — which are present at every value of both axes. Not one pixel of any tile is a rendered word naming its own variant. Billboard is disabled on all three, which also keeps LabelFramer out: it treats billboard-enabled as the hanging signal and would otherwise bolt a panel and a bezel behind each one, three slabs this quarry did not ask for. Label3D is not a MeshInstance3D and does not enter the capture AABB.

THE CAPTURE AABB IS THE REAL BODY. Every drawn node is a MeshInstance3D — BoxMesh for the apron, the wall, the datum rule and the rule marks, SurfaceTool ArrayMesh for each bench — so no `layers = 0` anchor is needed and none is present.

IF IT COMES BACK FAINT, check three things before the design.
(1) Was --max at least 12? At the gallery default of 9 a 3 x 4 declaration renders 3 x 3 and `octaves` is measured on [1, 2, 3] alone. That would make the number LARGER rather than smaller — the thinnest pair, 3<->4, is the one dropped — but it would be a verdict about three values published as a verdict about four.
(2) Was the sweep run --staged? A 4.20 m quarry is under the 6 m staging cut-off, so a plinth would be added under it, the pair AABB would grow and every mark would shrink.
(3) Is the standpoint doing the work? The three benches rank across the frame rather than in depth, so this artifact is less standpoint-sensitive than most — but the relief/column distinction lives entirely in an oblique view, and from directly overhead the two are the same picture. Per the standing gate an INERT verdict on this token is not reportable until tools/probe_anamorphic.py has been run on it.
